english: Let $\lambda$ be a real number, and let $\overrightarrow{u}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{v}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{w}=4\lambda\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. Suppose that the vector $3\hat{i}-\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ can be expressed in the form $x\overrightarrow{u}+y\overrightarrow{v}+z\overrightarrow{w}$, with real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$, in more than one way. Then the value of $\lambda$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $\lambda$ एक वास्तविक संख्या है, तथा $\overrightarrow{u}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{v}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ और $\overrightarrow{w}=4\lambda\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ हैं। माना कि सदिश $3\hat{i}-\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ को वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$, $y$, $z$ के साथ $x\overrightarrow{u}+y\overrightarrow{v}+z\overrightarrow{w}$ के रूप में एक से अधिक प्रकार से व्यक्त किया जा सकता है। तब $\lambda$ का मान ______ है।
solution: If $\overrightarrow{u},\overrightarrow{v},\overrightarrow{w}$ were non-coplanar the expression would be unique, so they are coplanar:
$\lambda=1$: last two equations give $-1=-4$, no solution, so rejected
$\lambda=\dfrac14$: subtracting, $\dfrac34x=3\Rightarrow x=4$, $y+z=-5$, and the first equation $8+y+z=3$ holds: infinitely many solutions
solution_full: If $\overrightarrow{u},\overrightarrow{v},\overrightarrow{w}$ are non-coplanar, every vector is a linear combination of them in exactly one way. So more than one expression forces them to be coplanar, i.e. $[\overrightarrow{u}\ \overrightarrow{v}\ \overrightarrow{w}]=0$.
So $\lambda=1$ or $\lambda=\dfrac14$. Coplanarity is necessary, not sufficient: the given vector must also lie in their plane.
Equating components of $x\overrightarrow{u}+y\overrightarrow{v}+z\overrightarrow{w}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ gives the system $2x+y+4\lambda z=3$, $x+y+z=-1$, $\lambda x+y+z=-4$.
For $\lambda=1$ the second and third equations read $x+y+z=-1$ and $x+y+z=-4$, which is inconsistent: no expression at all.
For $\lambda=\dfrac14$: the third equation is $\dfrac14x+y+z=-4$; subtracting it from the second gives $\dfrac34x=3$, so $x=4$ and $y+z=-5$.
The first equation becomes $8+y+z=3$, i.e. $y+z=-5$, the same condition. So $x=4$, $y=t$, $z=-5-t$ for every real $t$: infinitely many expressions.
originality_note: New: the non-uniqueness of a linear combination is turned into a parametric system whose determinant has two roots, one giving an inconsistent system and one a consistent one (way 5). Closest known: values of lambda for which three vectors are coplanar. Different because: coplanarity alone gives two values; the consistency of the system picks one, so the answer is not the usual 'roots of the determinant'.

concept_use.Linear combination theorem in space: Non-coplanar vectors give a unique expression, so non-uniqueness forces [u v w] = 0, i.e. lambda = 1 or 1/4.
concept_use.System of linear equations: The component system is inconsistent for lambda = 1 and has infinitely many solutions for lambda = 1/4 (consistency check).

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked ranks: lambda = 1 gives rank 2 versus augmented rank 3; lambda = 1/4 gives equal ranks 2, so exactly one value fits. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising that the determinant condition is only necessary and rejecting lambda = 1 by inconsistency.
justification: Two ideas linked: uniqueness of linear combinations and consistency of a singular system, with a trap root (lambda = 1) that a hurried student keeps. Comparable to the system casework of 2023-P1-Q14 (L1) but with the trap and numerical format; placed with 2026-P1-Q6 (L3).
